item.research_question: How can single-atom Mo tailoring and intrinsic tensile strain in high-entropy alloy nanosheets be utilized to enhance methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) activity, CO tolerance, and durability while avoiding CO poisoning?
item.material_system: Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn single-atom high-entropy-alloy (SAHEA) ultrathin nanosheets; atomic ratio Pd/Pt/Ni/Cu/Zn/Mo = 24.1/14.6/26.3/22.1/11.1/1.8; also senary Mo1-PdPtCoNiCuZn and septenary Mo1-PdPtFeCoNiCuZn SAHEA NSs
item.processing_route: One-pot liquid-phase synthesis at 200 °C using oleylamine (OAm) as solvent; precursors: Pt(acac)2, Pd(acac)2, Ni(acac)2, Zn(acac)2, Mo(CO)6, and L-ascorbic acid; Cu(acac)2 added dropwise after initial heating to 200 °C; reaction time 2 h; followed by cooling, centrifugation, and washing with cyclohexane/ethanol
item.test_conditions: Electrocatalytic tests in 1.0 M KOH + 1.0 M methanol; cyclic voltammetry at 50 mV s−1; chronoamperometry at 0.77 V vs. RHE for 10,000 s (and 10 h); CO stripping in N2-saturated 1.0 M KOH; in-situ FTIR from 0.2 V to 1.3 V vs. RHE
key_findings: Mass activity of 24.55 A mgPt−1 and 11.62 A mgPd+Pt−1, which are 18.13 and 8.58 times higher than commercial Pt/C, respectively
Specific activity of 16.55 mA cm−2, 7.13 times higher than commercial Pt/C
Average lattice spacing varies from 0.233 nm to 0.237 nm, indicating ~4.4% intrinsic tensile strain
Electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of 70.21 m2 g−1 for Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs
Current density remains 1.15 A mgPt−1 after 10 h of chronoamperometry testing
Onset potential for formate production is 0.45 V, 100 mV lower than that of commercial Pt/C (0.55 V)
No CO adsorbate (COads) signal observed in in-situ FTIR over the entire potential range
item.mechanism: The oxophilic Mo single atoms modify the electronic structure of isolated Pt sites, suppressing COads formation and steering the reaction toward a formate-dominated pathway; intrinsic tensile strain and Mo promoters synergistically optimize intermediate adsorption, lowering the energy barrier for the rate-determining step and facilitating deep oxidation of intermediates to CO2
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study
item.future_work: The authors propose that this work opens an encouraging pathway to the design of CO-tolerance electrocatalysts and demonstrates a general strategy for engineering-strained single atom-modified HEA catalysts for a wide range of applications
quotes: The as-made Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn delivers an extraordinary mass activity of 24.55 A mgPt−1 and 11.62 A mgPd+Pt−1, along with impressive long-term durability.

The planted oxophilic Mo single atoms as promoters modify the electronic structure of isolated Pt sites in the high-entropy-alloy host, suppressing the formation of CO adsorbates and steering the reaction towards the formate pathway.
The Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs can avoid the formation of COads and switch the MOR to the formate-dominated pathway

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can single-atom Mo tailoring and intrinsic tensile strain in high-entropy alloy nanosheets be utilized to enhance methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) activity, CO tolerance, and durability while avoiding CO poisoning?. System: Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn single-atom high-entropy-alloy (SAHEA) ultrathin nanosheets; atomic ratio Pd/Pt/Ni/Cu/Zn/Mo = 24.1/14.6/26.3/22.1/11.1/1.8; also senary Mo1-PdPtCoNiCuZn and septenary Mo1-PdPtFeCoNiCuZn SAHEA NSs. Processing: One-pot liquid-phase synthesis at 200 °C using oleylamine (OAm) as solvent; precursors: Pt(acac)2, Pd(acac)2, Ni(acac)2, Zn(acac)2, Mo(CO)6, and L-ascorbic acid; Cu(acac)2 added dropwise after initial heating to 200 °C; reaction time 2 h; followed by cooling, centrifugation, and washing with cyclohexane/ethanol. Test conditions: Electrocatalytic tests in 1.0 M KOH + 1.0 M methanol; cyclic voltammetry at 50 mV s−1; chronoamperometry at 0.77 V vs. RHE for 10,000 s (and 10 h); CO stripping in N2-saturated 1.0 M KOH; in-situ FTIR from 0.2 V to 1.3 V vs. RHE. Findings: Mass activity of 24.55 A mgPt−1 and 11.62 A mgPd+Pt−1, which are 18.13 and 8.58 times higher than commercial Pt/C, respectively; Specific activity of 16.55 mA cm−2, 7.13 times higher than commercial Pt/C; Average lattice spacing varies from 0.233 nm to 0.237 nm, indicating ~4.4% intrinsic tensile strain; Electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of 70.21 m2 g−1 for Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs; Current density remains 1.15 A mgPt−1 after 10 h of chronoamperometry testing; Onset potential for formate production is 0.45 V, 100 mV lower than that of commercial Pt/C (0.55 V); No CO adsorbate (COads) signal observed in in-situ FTIR over the entire potential range. Mechanism: The oxophilic Mo single atoms modify the electronic structure of isolated Pt sites, suppressing COads formation and steering the reaction toward a formate-dominated pathway; intrinsic tensile strain and Mo promoters synergistically optimize intermediate adsorption, lowering the energy barrier for the rate-determining step and facilitating deep oxidation of intermediates to CO2. Limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study. Future work: The authors propose that this work opens an encouraging pathway to the design of CO-tolerance electrocatalysts and demonstrates a general strategy for engineering-strained single atom-modified HEA catalysts for a wide range of applications. Quote: "The as-made Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn delivers an extraordinary mass activity of 24.55 A mgPt−1 and 11.62 A mgPd+Pt−1, along with impressive long-term durability."
